reference: Independent python implementation of every cycle the page offers (component-by-component first and second law, written from the textbook definitions), plus law-based invariants — loop energy balance, component entropy generation, isentropic-efficiency direction and the Carnot bound — evaluated from the numbers the page itself prints. CoolProp 8.0.0 supplies the fluid properties on both sides, so property agreement is a check that the WebAssembly binding is wired correctly, not an independent property check.
reference_citations: M. J. Moran, H. N. Shapiro, D. D. Boettner, M. B. Bailey, Fundamentals of Engineering Thermodynamics, 8th ed., ch. 8 (vapour power systems: Rankine, reheat, regenerative with open feedwater heaters) and ch. 10 (vapour-compression refrigeration, flash-chamber two-stage, transcritical CO2) — component definitions of isentropic turbine/pump/compressor efficiency, open-feedwater-heater bleed fractions and flash-tank mass/energy balances.
Y. A. Cengel, M. A. Boles, Thermodynamics: An Engineering Approach, 8th ed., §10-6 (regenerative Rankine with open FWH) and §11-2/11-6 (vapour-compression and cascade/multistage systems).

Second law as applied here: Clausius inequality per adiabatic component (s_out >= s_in) and the Carnot limit eta <= 1 - T_sink/T_source, COP_c <= T_c/(T_h-T_c), evaluated with the temperatures the page itself reports.
CoolProp 8.0.0 (python) — property source shared with the page WebAssembly build; used for the binding check and as the property layer of the reference.
tolerance: Every graded quantity is compared at the precision the page prints it: efficiency and bleed fraction to 0.05 % (one decimal shown), COP to 0.005 (two decimals), power/duty cards to half of the last printed digit (0.5 MW, 0.05 MW or 0.005 MW by magnitude; 0.5 kW / 0.05 kW / 50 kW for the refrigeration cards), state-point enthalpy to 0.05 kJ/kg, entropy to 5e-5 kJ/(kg K), temperature to 0.05 K, plus 2e-6 relative for the property round-trips both implementations perform. Law-based invariants are graded at the propagated display tolerance of the numbers they combine; an entropy difference between two printed entropies can only be resolved to 1.05e-4 kJ/(kg K) (two values each rounded to four decimals), so that is the slack allowed on entropy generation, while the Carnot bound is required with no slack at all. Input-consistency checks (the state points must sit at the temperatures the user typed) are graded to 0.051 K, the display resolution. Refusal cases pass only if the page shows a message AND clears the previous result — an error banner over a stale state table is graded as a failure. Quantities on which CoolProp 8.0.0 and 7.2.0 disagree by more than the tolerance are flagged and not graded.

reasons: input_T_evaporating: R410A is modelled as a pseudo-pure blend: the page takes the evaporating/condensing temperature as the dew point, so a two-phase state at that pressure sits at the bubble point about 0.1 K lower (temperature glide, not resolved by the pseudo-pure model)

crosscheck: Every reference quantity is computed with both property-library versions. Worst mutual deviation 1.014e-02 (ihx02.pts.5.v). Quantities where the two versions disagree by more than the grading tolerance are flagged in the result file and are not graded, per the harness rule on disagreeing references. Property layer: CoolProp 8.0.0 (python); crosscheck: CoolProp 7.2.0 (python, separate virtualenv) — the version whose equations of state match the WebAssembly build shipped with the page (CoolProp 7.2.1dev).
not_benchmarked: The fluid properties themselves. The page runs CoolProp (7.2.1dev) as WebAssembly and the reference uses CoolProp from python, so property agreement here only shows that the WebAssembly binding is wired correctly (same fluid, same state, same numbers) — it is not an independent check of the equations of state. Water/steam properties are benchmarked independently against IAPWS-IF97 in the steam-tables artifact.

The drawn diagram: the saturation dome, the isobars, isotherms and quality lines are read for crashes and for the fail-fast behaviour of the property calls, but the pixel geometry of the plot is not graded.

Otto, Diesel, Brayton and Stirling cycles: the page does not implement them (the manifest text that claimed an Otto cycle was corrected in this pass), so the closed-form ideal-cycle efficiencies were derived but had nothing to grade against.
Off-design behaviour, machine performance maps, pressure drops, heat-exchanger sizing and mechanical/electrical losses: outside the model.
Zeotropic mixtures other than the pseudo-pure R410A treatment, and the temperature glide of R410A itself.
run_notes: Driven through the page DOM over http://127.0.0.1:8099 (the page fetches its 6.5 MB CoolProp WebAssembly core, thermodynamiccycles.wasm, so file:// cannot be used), Chromium via Playwright, one page for the whole run.

Every case is graded twice: against the independent python implementation of the cycle (component-by-component first law with the textbook isentropic-efficiency definitions, open-feedwater-heater bleed balances and flash-tank mass/energy balance), and against law-based invariants computed only from the numbers the page prints — loop energy balance, component entropy generation, the isentropic efficiency recovered from the printed enthalpies, the lever rule between three printed two-phase states, COP_h = COP_c + 1, the input temperatures, and the Carnot bound between the actual source and sink temperature.

Before this pass the same harness reported 45/57. The failures were: a renderer crash on R410A (the WebAssembly build dies after a few hundred caught property exceptions, and the quality lines produced ~1080 of them per redraw), five inputs that were accepted although they are unphysical (turbine efficiency above 1 or equal to 0, compressor efficiency above 1, internal-heat-exchanger effectiveness above 1, a turbine inlet below the saturation temperature), three out-of-range pressures that were silently clamped instead of refused, and eleven cases where an error banner was shown while the previous cycle stayed on screen.
Page errors captured during the run: none.
